s: The Gupta Era of 319 AD is linked with which ruler?
x: The Gupta Era of 319 AD is linked with Chandragupta I and the start of the imperial phase, though Srigupta founded the dynasty.

s: The Vikrama Samvat is ahead of the Saka Samvat by how many years?
x: Vikrama equals Saka plus 135 years (57 BC versus 78 AD).

s: Which era is correctly matched with its starting year?
x: The Kalachuri/Chedi Era began in 248 AD; Vikrama Samvat in 57/58 BC, the Kali Era in 3102 BC and the Harsha Era in 606 AD.

s: In which year did the Kali era begin?
x: The Kali era traditionally begins in 3102 BC; 57 BC is Vikrama, 78 AD Saka and 248 AD Kalachuri.

s: In which year did the Harsha era, marking Harshavardhana's accession, begin?
x: The Harsha era began in 606 AD; 319 AD is Gupta, 248 AD Kalachuri and 1119 AD Lakshmana Sena.

s: By what other names is the Vikrama Samvat, traditionally linked with victory over the Sakas, known?
x: Krit Samvat and Malav Samvat are other names of the Vikrama Samvat.

s: Who is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Vikrama Samvat?
x: The Vikrama Samvat (57 BC) is credited to Vikramaditya of Ujjain and linked with a victory over the Sakas.

s: Besides Kanishka's coronation, the beginning of the Saka era (78 AD) is also equated with the accession of which ruler?
x: The Saka era is keyed to Kanishka but is also equated with the accession of the Kardamaka ruler Chashtana.

s: From which date was the Saka era adopted as the national calendar of India?
x: The Saka calendar, whose first month is Chaitra, was adopted as the national calendar from 22 March 1957.

s: On which date does 1 Chaitra of the national calendar fall in a leap year?
x: 1 Chaitra is 22 March in a normal year and 21 March in a leap year.

s: Which is the first month of the Indian national calendar based on the Saka era?
x: The national calendar (from 22 March 1957) begins with Chaitra; 1 Chaitra falls on 22 March (21 March in a leap year).

s: What number must be added to a Saka year to convert it into the AD year?
x: The AD year is the Saka year plus 78 (not 77), since the Saka era began in 78 AD.

s: From which city did Rudradaman I rule, c. 130-150 CE?
x: Rudradaman I, a Kardamaka, ruled from Ujjain.

s: Why is the Junagadh rock inscription of Rudradaman I significant?
o: The first copper-plate charter of the Guptas
The earliest inscription entirely in Tamil
The first long inscription in Sanskrit
x: The Junagadh or Girnar record is regarded as the first long inscription in Sanskrit; earlier long records were generally in Prakrit.

s: Who originally built the Sudarshana lake?
x: Pushyagupta built the lake, Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka, Rudradaman repaired it through Suvishakha and Chakrapalita repaired it in the Gupta period.

s: Which Pahlava minister of Rudradaman I repaired the Sudarshana lake?
x: Suvishakha repaired the lake for Rudradaman I; Pushyagupta built it, Tushaspha added canals and Chakrapalita repaired it later.

s: Who added canals to the Sudarshana lake during Ashoka's reign?
x: The Yavanaraja Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka.

s: In whose reign did Chakrapalita repair the Sudarshana lake?
x: Chakrapalita, son of governor Parnadatta, repaired the lake in the Gupta period under Skandagupta.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I?
o: It records victories over Satakarni and the Yaudheyas
It is the first long inscription in Prakrit
It records the repair of Sudarshana lake
x: It is the first long inscription in Sanskrit; earlier long records were in Prakrit.

s: Which inscription records Rudradaman I's two victories over Satakarni and the repair of the Sudarshana lake?
x: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman I, dated Saka 72, records his victories over Satakarni and the repair of Sudarshana lake.

s: Rudradaman I's Junagadh inscription is dated Saka 72. Which year of the Common Era does this correspond to?
x: Saka 72 = 72 + 78 = 150 CE; Rudradaman ruled c. 130-150 CE from Ujjain.

s:
Consider the following statements about the foreign groups in ancient India:
1. The Indo-Greeks appeared before the Sakas.
2. The Parthians appeared before the Sakas.
3. The Kushanas appeared after the Parthians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order was Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Parthians and Kushanas, so statement 2 is wrong: the Parthians came after the Sakas.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Rajuvula and Sodasa belonged to the Mathura branch. The Upper Deccan branch was associated with the Kshaharatas Bhumaka and Nahapana.

s: As what were the Sakas absorbed into Indian society?
x: The Sakas were absorbed into society as Vratya Kshatriyas and ruled through Satrapas and Mahasatrapas.

s: Mathura, Ujjain and Girnar were centres of the rule of which people?
x: Mathura, Ujjain and Girnar were Saka centres; the Sakas were often at war with the Satavahanas.

s: Patika, known from the Taxila copper plate, belonged to the Shaka branch centred at which place?
x: Liaka Kusulaka and Patika ruled the north-western Shaka branch at Taxila.

s: Where was the Shaka branch ruled by Rajuvula and Sodasa centred?
x: Rajuvula and Sodasa were Shaka rulers of Mathura.

s: Under which titles did the Saka rulers govern in India?
x: The Sakas ruled through the satrap system as Satrapas and Mahasatrapas.

s: According to Christian tradition, St Thomas visited the court of which ruler?
x: Tradition says St Thomas visited the court of Gondophares, the greatest Parthian (Pahlava) ruler, associated with the Takht-i-Bahi inscription.

s: With which Parthian ruler is the Takht-i-Bahi inscription associated?
x: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription belongs to Gondophares, the greatest Parthian ruler, not to a Saka ruler.

s: Near which place was the Takht-i-Bahi inscription of Gondophares found?
x: Takht-i-Bahi lies near Peshawar.

s: For which military arm were the Shakas, Parthians and Kushanas known?
x: These groups are known for better cavalry, not elephant armies; the Shakas and Kushanas also introduced trousers, long coats, helmets and boots.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Shakas and Kushanas:
1. They introduced trousers, long coats, helmets and boots.
2. Their military strength lay mainly in elephants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: They introduced trousers, long coats, helmets and boots; their military edge was better cavalry, not elephants.

s: Who is generally identified as the first prominent Saka king in India?
x: Maues, also known as Moga, is regarded as the first prominent Saka king, around 80 BC.

s: Where did the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas rule?
x: The Kshaharatas held the Western Deccan, while the Kardamakas ruled around Ujjain, Malwa and Kathiawar.

s: Bhumaka and Nahapana belonged to which Shaka branch?
x: Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas of Nasik; Chashtana and Rudradaman I were Kardamakas.

s: To which branch of the Western Kshatrapas did Chashtana and Rudradaman I belong?
x: Chashtana and Rudradaman I were Kardamakas ruling Kathiawar and Malwa from Ujjain; Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas.

s: The clash between Chashtana and Vasishthiputra Pulumavi is referred to by which ancient writer?
x: Ptolemy records the clash between Chashtana and the Satavahana ruler Vasishthiputra Pulumavi.

s: Rudradaman I's defeat of Pulumavi is associated with which change in Satavahana political geography?
o: The transfer of the centre from Amaravati to Pratishthana
The transfer of the centre from Amaravati to Junagadh
The transfer of the centre from Paithan to Junagadh
The transfer of the centre from Pratishthana to Amaravati
x: Following Rudradaman I's defeat of Pulumavi, the Satavahana centre shifted from Pratishthana, or Paithan, to Amaravati.

s: Who issued the Nasik Prashasti, which calls Gautamiputra Satakarni the destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas?
x: The Nasik Prashasti was issued by Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni. Naganika is linked with the Nanaghat inscription, Ushavadatta with Nahapana's Nasik and Karle records, and Rudradamanika was Rudradaman's daughter.

s: Rudradaman I's daughter married which Satavahana ruler?
x: Rudradaman's daughter married Vasishthiputra Satakarni; because of this close relationship Rudradaman spared Satakarni after defeating him twice.

s: Which Satavahana ruler defeated Nahapana of the Kshaharata dynasty and restruck his coins?
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Kshaharata ruler Nahapana and restruck his coins as an assertion of Satavahana power.

s: The Jogalthembi hoard is particularly associated with which of the following?
o: Restruck silver coins of Nahapana by Gautamiputra Satakarni
x: The Jogalthembi hoard contains silver coins of Nahapana restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni.

s: Ushavadatta, who deposited money with the weavers' guild at Govardhana, was the son-in-law of whom?
x: Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law; his Nasik record deposits money with the weavers' guild at Govardhana at 12% a year.

s: Who made the gift of a village to the monks of the Karle chaitya?
x: The Karle inscription records Ushavadatta's gift of a village to the monks; Junnar belongs to Ayama.

s: At what annual rate of interest did Ushavadatta deposit money with the Govardhana weavers' guild?
x: The Nasik record says 2,000 karshapanas were deposited with the weavers' guild at 12% a year.

s: What was the relation of Ayama, who issued the Junnar (Manmodi) cave inscription, to Nahapana?
x: Ayama was Nahapana's minister (amatya); Ushavadatta was his son-in-law.

s: Which inscription records the gift of a cave by Ayama, the minister of Nahapana, dated year 46?
x: Ayama, Nahapana's amatya, recorded the gift of a cave/mandapa at Junnar (Manmodi) in year 46.

s:
Consider the following about Western Kshatrapa coinage:
1. Their principal coins were exclusively gold.
2. Their silver coins are numerous in western India.
3. Kardamaka silver coins carried Saka-era dates.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Numerous Western Kshatrapa silver coins are found in western India and Kardamaka silver coins bear Saka-era dates; their coinage was not exclusively gold.

s: Who compiled the Mahavibhasha at the Fourth Buddhist Council?
x: The Mahavibhasha was compiled by Vasumitra, the council's president; Ashvaghosha was vice-president.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Fourth Buddhist Council?
o: It was held at Kundalvana in Kashmir
x: Vasumitra was the president of the Fourth Buddhist Council; Ashvaghosha was its vice-president.

s: Where was the Second Buddhist Council held?
x: The Second Council met at Vaishali; the First was at Rajagriha, the Third at Pataliputra and the Fourth in Kashmir.

s: Who was the vice-president of the Fourth Buddhist Council?
x: Ashvaghosha was vice-president; Vasumitra presided over the Council.

s: Where was the Fourth Buddhist Council held?
x: The Fourth Council met at Kundalvana (Harwan) in Kashmir under Kanishka, not at Pataliputra.

s: In which language were the proceedings of the Fourth Buddhist Council held?
x: The Fourth Council was the first in Sanskrit; earlier councils used Pali or Prakrit.

s: Who was the court physician of Kanishka?
x: Charaka was Kanishka's court physician; Ashvaghosha was his poet laureate and Vasumitra headed the Fourth Council.

s: Which scholar is associated with Madhyamika philosophy and the work Suhrllekha?
x: Nagarjuna is associated with Madhyamika philosophy and Suhrllekha, a letter addressed to a Satavahana king.

s: Nagarjuna, associated with the Madhyamika school, is linked in Andhra history with which of the following?
x: Nagarjuna of the Madhyamika school is associated with Sriparvata and the Satavahana court in Andhra.

s: What did I-tsing say about Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha?
o: Recited only at the Satavahana court
x: I-tsing recorded that he saw students in India memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha.

s: Which scholar of Kanishka's court urged the holding of the Fourth Buddhist Council?
x: Parshva, a Buddhist scholar, urged Kanishka to hold the Council.

s: Which scholar of the Kushana period is called the 'Einstein of India'?
x: Nagarjuna, the Madhyamika philosopher and author of Suhrllekha, is called the 'Einstein of India'.

s: Under the Kushanas, Buddhism shifted from Pali-Prakrit Hinayana to which form?
x: The Kushana shift was to Sanskrit Mahayana, whose followers made images of the Buddha and worshipped him as a god.

s: To which regions did Buddhism spread in the Kushana period?
o: Central Asia, China, Korea and Japan
x: Buddhism spread to Central Asia, China, Korea and Japan in this period.

s: At which site in Kashmir were stupas showing the valley's Gandhara Buddhist heritage highlighted in 2026?
x: Stupas at Zehanpora in Kashmir show the valley's Gandhara Buddhist heritage (2026).

s:
Which of the following works are attributed to Ashvaghosha?
1. Saundarananda
2. Buddhacharita
3. Sariputraprakarana
Select the correct answer:
x: Saundarananda, Buddhacharita and Sariputraprakarana are all works of Ashvaghosha.

s: Kushana trade contributed to which development in India?
o: The beginning of the Sangam Age
The decline of Mathura and Taxila
x: Kushana trade promoted a second wave of urbanisation involving centres such as Mathura, Taxila, Ujjain and Shravasti.

s: The Kushanas played the role of middlemen in trade linking which of the following regions?
x: The Kushanas acted as Silk Road intermediaries connecting Han China, Rome and India.

s: The Kushanas belonged to which people?
x: The Kushanas were Yueh-chi (Yuezhi) from north-west China and Central Asia.

s: Who united the five Yuezhi clans and took the Kabul valley and Kashmir?
x: Kujula Kadphises (Kadphises I) united the five clans; Vima Kadphises (Kadphises II) extended the empire to Mathura and Varanasi.

s: Who was the last great Kushana ruler?
x: Vasudeva I was the last great Kushan; Kanishka represented the zenith and Huvishka was his successor.

s: Which of the following sequences represents the genealogy given in the Rabatak inscription?
o: Kujula Kadphises → Vima Taktu → Vima Kadphises → Kanishka
Vima Taktu → Kujula Kadphises → Kanishka → Vima Kadphises
Kanishka → Vima Kadphises → Vima Taktu → Kujula Kadphises
Kujula Kadphises → Kanishka → Huvishka → Vima Taktu
x: The Rabatak inscription gives the succession as Kujula Kadphises, Vima Taktu, Vima Kadphises and Kanishka.

s: From where did the Kushana royal title 'Devaputra' come?
x: Devaputra reflected Chinese influence, Shaonano Shao Persian, Kaisara Roman and Maharaja Indian traditions.

s: From where did Kanishka's title 'Kaisara' come?
x: Kaisara (Caesar) came from Rome; Devaputra from China, Shaonano Shao from Persia and Maharaja from India.

s: Vima Kadphises, who took the title Sarvaloka Ishvara, was the father of whom?
x: Vima Kadphises was the father of Kanishka.

s: Which Kushana ruler, a devotee of Shiva, took the titles 'Maheshvara' and 'Sarvaloka Ishvara'?
x: Vima Kadphises (Kadphises II), a Shiva devotee, called himself Maheshvara and Sarvaloka Ishvara (RPSC 2024). Kujula united the Yuezhi clans, Kanishka took Devaputra and the other titles, and Huvishka was Kanishka's successor.

s: Who succeeded Kanishka on the Kushana throne?
x: Huvishka succeeded Kanishka, with Mathura as a major centre; Vasudeva I was the last great Kushana.

s: From which country did Kanishka's title 'Shaonano Shao' come?
x: Shaonano Shao (king of kings) is Persian; Devaputra is Chinese, Kaisara Roman and Maharaja Indian.

s: Which Kushana ruler extended the empire up to Mathura and Varanasi?
x: Vima Kadphises, father of Kanishka, extended the empire to Mathura and Varanasi.

s:
Which of the following cities are mentioned in the Rabatak inscription?
1. Saketa
2. Kaushambi
3. Sri Champa
Select the correct answer:
x: The Rabatak inscription says Kanishka's rule reached Saketa, Kaushambi, Pataliputra and Sri Champa.

s: What was Kanishka's main (winter) capital?
x: Purushapura (Peshawar) was the main/winter capital; Mathura was another capital and Surkh Kotal only a provincial centre.

s:
Consider the following about Kanishka and China:
1. Chinese texts call Kanishka's people the Yue-chi.
2. The Kushanas defeated the Chinese force of Pan Chao in 86 AD.
3. The Kushanas marched against Pan Chao after a Han princess was refused to Kanishka.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: After a Han princess was refused to Kanishka, the Kushanas (the Yue-chi of Chinese texts) marched against Pan Chao in 86 AD and lost to a smaller Chinese force.

s: Which of the following about the Rabatak inscription is correctly matched?
x: The Rabatak inscription was found near Surkh Kotal in Afghanistan in 1993; it uses the Greek script and the Bactrian language.

s: In which language and script is the Rabatak inscription of Kanishka written?
x: The Rabatak inscription is in the Bactrian language written in Greek script.

s: Who dedicated the Sarnath Bodhisattva image in year 3 of Kanishka?
x: Friar Bala dedicated the Sarnath Bodhisattva image in year 3 of Kanishka (81 AD).

s: In which year was the Rabatak inscription discovered in Afghanistan?
x: The Rabatak inscription was found in 1993 near Surkh Kotal, Afghanistan.

s: The era of 78 CE is usually credited to Kanishka, but some accounts credit which ruler with starting the Salivahana era?
x: Some accounts credit Gautamiputra Satakarni with starting the Salivahana era, though the 78 CE era is commonly credited to Kanishka.

s: Why did the era beginning in 78 CE come to be called the Saka era?
o: The Western Kshatrapas in their records and coins
x: The Western Kshatrapas, who were Sakas, used the era on their records and coins, so it became known as the Saka era.

s: By what other name is the era beginning in 78 CE known?
x: The era of 78 CE is also called Salivahana Saka and became India's national calendar in 1957.

s:
Consider the following about the Saka Samvat:
1. It began 135 years before the Vikrama era.
2. Many historians consider Kanishka its originator, beginning in 78 AD.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Many historians credit Kanishka with starting the Saka era in 78 AD; it began 135 years after, not before, the Vikrama era (57 BCE).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evidence for Kushana-period ports and trade?
o: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea is a written account of the ports of the period.
Arikamedu is an excavated site giving evidence of trade in the period.
Inamgaon is the excavated site paired with the Periplus as evidence of the period's ports.
Both a written account and an excavation attest the trade of the period.
x: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea and the Arikamedu excavation are the evidence for the ports and trading centres of the period; Inamgaon is not.

s: What was the Roman weight standard followed by the Kushana gold dinara?
x: The dinara followed the Roman standard of about 8 g (120 grains) and was 22-23 carat gold.

s: How is Kanishka shown on his coins?
o: Seated under a Bodhi tree with a manuscript
Standing in a peaked helmet, long coat and boots, sacrificing at an altar
Seated on a couch playing the veena
x: Kanishka stands in a peaked helmet, long coat and boots, sacrificing at an altar; Kushana coins carry 30+ Greek, Iranian and Indian deities.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Six-headed Kartikeya on coins – Vima Kadphises
x: Six-headed Kartikeya with a peacock appears on Yaudheya copper coins, not on those of Vima Kadphises.

s: About how many deities, Greek, Iranian and Indian, appear on Kushana coins?
x: Kushana coins show 30+ deities such as Helios, Mithra, Nana, Shiva with Nandi and the Buddha.

s: How did the Manusmriti describe the Shakas and Kushans who did not follow priestly customs?
x: The Manusmriti called Shakas, Kushans, Hunas and Pratiharas who did not follow priestly customs 'Fallen Kshatriyas'.

s: In which material are the narrative panels of the Amaravati school of art carved?
x: Amaravati is known for narrative panels in white limestone; the first Buddha images of the 1st century CE were in the Gandhara and Mathura styles.

s:
Consider the following statements about early Buddha images:
1. The Gandhara school shows a standing Buddha in pleated robes.
2. The Mathura school shows a seated Buddha with a halo.
3. The Amaravati school used red sandstone for its narrative panels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gandhara shows a standing Buddha and Mathura a seated one with a halo; Amaravati panels are of white limestone, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Which of the following items of dress was introduced into India by the Shakas and Kushanas?
x: The Shakas and Kushanas introduced trousers, heavy long coats, helmets and boots.

s: Which military development is associated with the Shakas and Kushanas?
o: Improved cavalry and wider use of saddles and reins
x: The Shakas and Kushanas improved cavalry and promoted the wider use of saddles and reins.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gandhara school of art:
1. It flourished in the north-west around Peshawar, Taxila and Swat.
2. Its main medium was spotted red sandstone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gandhara grew in the north-west around Peshawar, Taxila and Swat and used grey schist; spotted red sandstone was Mathura's medium.

s: Heavy, toga-like drapery on the Buddha is a feature of which school of art?
x: Gandhara shows heavy, toga-like drapery; Mathura shows transparent, clinging robes.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wavy hair with a top-knot – Gandhara
x: Wavy hair with a top-knot is Gandhara's; toga-like drapery is Gandhara's, clinging drapery and the Jnanachakra halo are Mathura's.

s: Besides grey schist, which material did the Gandhara school use in its later phase?
x: Gandhara used grey (green) schist and later stucco; red sandstone is Mathura and white limestone Amaravati.

s: Which of the following sets of influences is associated with Gandhara art?
x: Gandhara art reflects Hellenistic Greek, Roman and Persian influences in combination with Indian artistic traditions.

s: Which of the following was a centre of the Gandhara school of art?
x: Taxila, with Peshawar and the Swat Valley, was a Gandhara centre; the others belong to the Mathura and Amaravati schools.

s:
Consider the following about Gandhara art:
1. It predominantly expressed Mahayana Buddhism.
2. It represented the Buddha only through symbols.
3. It commonly depicted Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Gandhara art mainly expressed Mahayana Buddhism and showed the Buddha with Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya, not only through symbols.

s: Gupta stone sculpture is regarded as a continuation of which school of art?
x: The Mathura tradition continued in the Gupta period with greater elegance and softness, so Gupta stone sculpture belongs to the Mathura school.

s: With which form of representing the Buddha is Hinayana associated?
x: Hinayana is associated with symbolic worship, while Mahayana encouraged worship of Buddha images.

s:
Consider the following about the anthropomorphic Buddha image:
1. The Buddha was first widely shown in human form in the Kushana period.
2. Whether Gandhara or Mathura made the first such image is debated.
3. Only Amaravati produced the first anthropomorphic Buddha image.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both Gandhara and Mathura produced Buddha images in human form in the Kushana period (1st century CE), and their priority is debated; Amaravati was not the first.

s: How was the Buddha represented before human images became established?
o: Symbols such as throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa
x: Before anthropomorphic images, the Buddha was worshipped aniconically through the throne, footprints, wheel, tree and stupa.

s: Who introduced symbol worship (Chaitika Vada) in Andhra?
x: Mahadeva introduced Chaitika Vada in Andhra; the Amaravati Ayakapatas show the Buddha through symbols, not in human form.

s: How do the Ayakapatas of the Amaravati school show the Buddha?
x: Amaravati Ayakapatas represent the Buddha through symbols, not in human form.

s: What does the Dharmachakra mudra of the Buddha represent?
x: Dharmachakra mudra symbolises the turning of the wheel of law and is associated with the Buddha’s first sermon at Sarnath.

s: Which mudra is represented by the Buddha touching the earth with the right hand?
x: Bhumisparsha mudra shows the right hand touching the earth, symbolising enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and calling the earth to witness against Mara.

s: Which mudra of the Buddha shows a lowered open palm, the gesture of boon-giving?
x: Varada is the lowered open palm of boon-giving; Abhaya is the raised right palm and Dhyana the hands in the lap.

s: What does the Abhaya mudra (raised right palm) of the Buddha symbolise?
x: Abhaya, the raised right palm, means fearlessness; Dhyana is meditation and Varada boon-giving.

s: Which mudra shows the Buddha with his hands in the lap?
x: Dhyana mudra, hands resting in the lap, stands for meditation.

s: In the Bhumisparsha mudra, against whom does the Buddha call the earth to witness?
x: Bhumisparsha marks the Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, with the earth as witness against Mara.

s: Which mudra of the Buddha is linked with the subduing of the elephant Nalagiri?
x: The Abhaya mudra (raised right palm) shows fearlessness and is linked with subduing Nalagiri.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the schools of art?
o: Mature-phase Amaravati is linked with the Kushanas
Mathura is linked with the Kushanas and continued into the Gupta age
Amaravati is linked with the Satavahanas and later Ikshvakus
Gandhara is linked with the Kushanas
x: Mature-phase Amaravati is linked with the Ikshvakus and Mahayana themes, not the Kushanas.

s: In which region did the Amaravati school of art flourish?
x: Gandhara was in the north-west, Mathura in the Ganga valley and Amaravati in Andhra.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mathura – Muscular, robust and smiling figures
Gandhara – Slender figures showing intense movement
x: Slender, dynamic and emotional figures are typical of Amaravati; Gandhara is known for realistic, Apollo-like faces and spiritual calm.

s: Of which of the following is the depiction of Yakshas and Gandharvas dancing around the Buddha characteristic?
x: Amaravati compositions are narrative, crowded and full of movement; Yakshas and Gandharvas are shown dancing around the Buddha.

s: What were the sculptors of the Amaravati school known as?
x: The sculptors of the Amaravati school were called Selavardhakulu.

s: Who patronised the Amaravati school of art?
x: Amaravati art grew under the Satavahanas and later the Ikshvakus; the Kushanas patronised Gandhara and Mathura.

s: The first depiction of Sati in Indian art is found in which context?
o: A Mathura royal portrait of the Gupta period
A Gandhara sculpture of the Kushana period
An Amaravati-school sculpture of the Ikshvaku period
x: The first depiction of Sati in Indian art is found in an Amaravati-school sculpture belonging to the Ikshvaku period.

s: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art forms the emblem of which State Government?
x: The Purna-Kumbha motif of Amaravati art is the emblem of the Andhra Pradesh State Government.

s: Who called Amaravati art the 'Epitome of Indian architecture'?
x: 'Epitome of Indian architecture' was James Fergusson's phrase; Percy Brown called it the pinnacle of Indian art.

s: Where is the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The oldest stupa in AP is Bhattiprolu; Nagarjunakonda was the main centre under the Ikshvakus and Ghantasala another main centre.

s: Who publicised Amaravati art through the work 'Tree and Serpent Worship'?
x: James Fergusson publicised Amaravati art in Tree and Serpent Worship and called it the 'Epitome of Indian architecture'.

s: To which regions did the influence of Amaravati art spread?
o: Sri Lanka, South-East Asia and later Gupta art
x: Amaravati art influenced Sri Lanka (especially Anuradhapura), South-East Asia and later Gupta art.

s: Which was the main centre of Amaravati-style art under the Ikshvakus?
x: Nagarjunakonda was the main centre under the Ikshvakus; Bhattiprolu is noted as the oldest stupa in AP.

s: Which of the following is NOT an Amaravati-style site?
x: Jaggayyapeta, Goli and Ghantasala are Amaravati-style sites in Andhra; Mat is the Mathura-school findspot of Kanishka's statue.

s:
Consider the following statements about writers on Amaravati art:
1. Percy Brown wrote 'Tree and Serpent Worship'.
2. Percy Brown described Amaravati art as 'dynamic beauty'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Percy Brown praised its 'dynamic beauty'; 'Tree and Serpent Worship' was written by James Fergusson.

s: By what other name was Amaravati, where the Buddha is believed to have first taught the Kalachakra, known?
x: Amaravati was Dhanyakataka; Pratishthana is Paithan and Vijayapuri is Nagarjunakonda.

s: To the period of which dynasty does the mature phase of the Amaravati school belong?
x: The mature phase of Amaravati art, with Mahayana themes, is Ikshvaku, not Kushana.

s: Which school of art is the only one to depict all the events of the Buddha's life?
x: The Amaravati school alone shows all the events of the Buddha's life in its narrative panels.

s: Apart from the Amaravati Museum, in which museum is a large part of the Amaravati sculptures kept?
x: Amaravati sculptures are split between the Amaravati Museum and the British Museum (news, May 2026).

s: Which of the following sites forms a Buddhist circuit with Amaravati and Bavikonda in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP Buddhist circuit of Feb 2026 links Amaravati, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda.

s: In which material were the sculptures of the Mathura school mainly made?
x: Mathura used spotted red sandstone; Gandhara used grey schist and later stucco, and Amaravati white Palnadu limestone.

s: The halo (Jnanachakra) behind the Buddha's head is a hallmark of which school of art?
x: The Jnanachakra halo is a Mathura feature; Gandhara figures wear heavy toga-like robes and have wavy hair with a top-knot.

s: Which school of art is described as indigenous and multi-religious?
x: Mathura is indigenous and multi-religious; Gandhara is foreign-influenced and Buddhist, and Amaravati indigenous and narrative.

s: In which material were the sculptures of the Amaravati school mainly carved?
x: Amaravati used white Palnadu limestone; schist and stucco were Gandhara materials and red sandstone Mathura's.

s: Transparent, clinging drapery and a fleshy, smiling figure characterise which school of art?
x: Mathura figures are muscular, smiling and fleshy in clinging drapery; Gandhara drapery is heavy and toga-like.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Amaravati school of art?
o: Its figures are slender, dynamic and emotional.
Its themes include the Jatakas and the life of the Buddha.
Its main medium was spotted red sandstone.
x: Amaravati used white limestone; spotted red sandstone was the medium of Mathura.

s: Standing Buddha images became prominent in which phase of the Mathura school?
x: Standing Buddha images became prominent in the Gupta phase of the Mathura school.

s: Which school of art produced some of the earliest surviving iconic images of Shiva, Vishnu and Surya?
x: The Mathura school produced early iconic images of Hindu deities, as well as Jain Tirthankaras and Yaksha-Yakshi figures.

s: Where was the headless standing statue of Kanishka found?
x: The headless standing statue of Kanishka, a Kushana royal portrait of the Mathura school, comes from Mat.

s: Images of Jain Tirthankaras and Yaksha-Yakshi figures are associated mainly with which school of art?
x: Mathura made Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical images, including Tirthankaras and Yaksha-Yakshi; Gandhara was Buddhist only.

s:
Arrange the following dynasties in the chronological order of their succession in Magadha:
A. Kanvas
B. Mauryas
C. Satavahanas
D. Sungas
x: The sequence is Mauryas, Sungas, Kanvas and then Satavahanas. Simuka is associated with the overthrow of the Kanvas.

s: What do the terms 'Andhras' and 'Andhrabhrityas', used in the Puranas for the Satavahanas, signify respectively?
o: Andhras and servants or feudatories of the Andhras
A royal dynasty and its conquered enemies
Two branches of the Mauryan dynasty
x: The Puranas refer to them as Andhras or Andhrabhrityas. Andhrabhrityas means ‘servants of the Andhras’ or Andhras who had earlier been feudatories.

s: Which dynasty succeeded the Satavahanas in Vidarbha?
x: The Vakatakas succeeded them in Vidarbha, the Ikshvakus in Andhra and the Abhiras in Maharashtra.

s: How did the Satavahanas rise to political power?
o: Began as feudatories of the Mauryas and became independent after the decline of Mauryan power
Were appointed governors by the Western Kshatrapas
Defeated the Kushanas in northern India
Succeeded the Guptas in the Deccan
x: The Satavahanas are described as having initially served as Mauryan feudatories and having established independence in the Deccan after the decline of the Mauryas.

s: Which is regarded as the first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan?
x: The Satavahanas are regarded as the first historical dynasty of the Deccan and a link between northern and southern India.

s: Simuka rose to power by overthrowing which dynasty?
x: Simuka ended the Kanvas, who followed the Sungas in Magadha.

s: Which successor of the Satavahanas ruled in Maharashtra?
x: The Abhiras succeeded in Maharashtra, the Vakatakas in Vidarbha and the Ikshvakus in Andhra.

s: Which Kanva king was defeated by a Satavahana king?
x: The Satavahanas ended Kanva rule; a Satavahana king defeated Kanva Susarma.

s: The restriking of whose silver coins by Gautamiputra Satakarni is evidenced by the Jogalthambi hoard?
x: The Jogalthambi hoard contains Nahapana’s silver coins restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni, providing evidence of Gautamiputra’s victory.

s: Ayama, the Kshaharata minister, is linked with which inscription?
x: Ayama, the minister, issued the Junnar inscription; Ushavadata was Nahapana's son-in-law.

s:
Consider the following about Gautamiputra Satakarni:
1. He belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
2. He defeated Nahapana and recovered Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and recovered these territories; it was Nahapana who belonged to the Kshaharata branch.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the territories Gautamiputra Satakarni regained from Nahapana?
x: He regained Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik from Nahapana; Kalinga was not among them.

s: To which period is Gautamiputra Satakarni dated?
x: Gautamiputra ruled c. 106-130 CE, so crediting him with the Saka/Salivahana era of AD 78 does not fit.

s: What is the principal source for the reign of Gautamiputra Satakarni?
x: The Nasik Prasasti is the main source for Gautamiputra's reign, while the Satavahana homeland and chronology remain debated.

s: Mahishmati was the capital of which territory mentioned in the Nasik Prasasti?
x: Anupa represented the Narmada valley and its capital was Mahishmati.

s: The Nasik Prasasti, in Prakrit prose and Brahmi script, praises which ruler as destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas?
x: The Nasik Prasasti records Gautamiputra Satakarni's expeditions, victories, empire and titles, including his destruction of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.

s: According to the Nasik record, near which place did Gautamiputra Satakarni gift a village to monks?
x: The Nasik record notes a village near Trirashmi gifted to monks and 100 nivartanas of his own land.

s: To which modern region does Akara of the Nasik Prasasti correspond?
x: Akara was East Malwa; Avanti was West Malwa, Aparanta North Konkan and Vidarbha Berar.

s: The Nasik Prasasti presents Gautamiputra Satakarni as belonging to which varna?
x: Balasri’s account presents Gautamiputra’s line as Brahmana. The inscription also describes him as the crusher of Kshatriya pride.

s: The Nasik Prasasti was issued in which regnal year of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi?
x: Gautami Balasri issued it in the 19th regnal year of her grandson Vasishthiputra Pulumavi.

s: What does Gautamiputra Satakarni's title 'Varnasankarya-nirodhaka' mean?
o: Crusher of the pride of the Kshatriyas
Stopper of the mixing of varnas
Whose horses drank the waters of three seas
x: Varnasankarya-nirodhaka means he stopped the mixing of the varnas; Ekabrahmana means unique Brahmana.

s: To which modern region does Aparanta, named in the Nasik Prasasti, correspond?
x: Aparanta is North Konkan; Anupa is the Narmada valley, Vidarbha is Berar and Akara is East Malwa.

s:
Match the following regions of the Nasik Prasasti with their modern areas:
List-I
A. Anupa
B. Vidarbha
C. Avanti
D. Aparanta
List-II
1. Berar
2. Narmada valley
3. West Malwa
4. North Konkan
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Anupa = Narmada valley (capital Mahishmati), Vidarbha = Berar, Avanti = West Malwa, Aparanta = North Konkan.

s: Which of the following title – meaning pairs of Gautamiputra Satakarni is correctly matched?
o: Ekabrahmana – Crusher of the pride of the Kshatriyas
Kshatriya-darpa-mana-mardana – Crusher of the pride of the Kshatriyas
Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana – Lord of the southern sea
x: Kshatriya-darpa-mana-mardana means crusher of Kshatriya pride; Ekabrahmana is unique Brahmana and Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana means his horses drank the waters of three seas.

s: Where was the Jogalthambi hoard of Nahapana's coins restruck by Gautamiputra found?
x: The Jogalthambi hoard is from Nasik district and confirms Gautamiputra's victory.

s: During the reign of which grandson did Gautami Balasri issue the Nasik inscription?
x: Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik inscription in the reign of her grandson Pulumavi; Naganika is linked with the Naneghat inscription.

s: How many coins did the Jogalthambi hoard contain?
x: The Jogalthambi hoard had 13,270 coins; 3,730 is the Ikshvaku Phanigiri pot.

s: Which Satavahana king gave a village at Tirasmri and 100 nivartanas of land to Buddhist monks?
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni gifted a village at Tirasmri and 100 nivartanas to monks.

s: What do Satavahana metronymics such as 'Gautamiputra' show?
o: Foundation of the dynasty by a queen
Election of kings by the queen mothers
The high status of royal women, with succession remaining patriarchal
x: Metronymics reflected the high status of royal women and respect for the mother, while succession stayed patriarchal.

s: Who was Gautami Balasri?
o: The regent of Yajna Sri Satakarni during his minority
The queen of Hala who composed Gathasaptasati
The queen mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni who built a Nasik cave for Bhadrayaniya monks
The wife of Satakarni I who issued the Naneghat inscription
x: Gautami Balasri was the mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni. She built a Nasik cave for Bhadrayaniya monks, and her Nasik Prasasti glorified her son.

s:
Consider the following about Satavahana queens:
1. Devi Naganika acted as regent during her son's minority.
2. Naganika was the queen of Hala.
3. Naganika was the wife of Satakarni I.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, acted as regent during her son's minority; Lilavati was Hala's queen.

s: Lilavati, a Sri Lankan princess, was the queen of which Satavahana king?
x: Lilavati was Hala's queen, not Gautamiputra's.

s: Gautami Balasri built a cave at Nasik for which group of monks?
x: She built a Nasik cave for the Bhadrayaniya monks; the Karle village went to the Mahasanghikas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Satavahana metronymics?
o: Kings prefixed their mother's gotra name to their own.
They show the high status of royal women.
x: Metronymics show respect for royal mothers, but succession stayed patriarchal.

s: Devi Naganika, the queen of Satakarni I, was the daughter of whom?
x: Naganika was the daughter of Maharathi Tranakayiro; she issued the Naneghat inscription.

s: What is the usual explanation for the Satavahana practice of prefixing the mother's name to the king's name?
o: Polygamy, so princes were told apart by their mothers
x: Metronymics are usually explained by polygamy; succession itself stayed patriarchal.

s: What is the use of maternal gotra names by Satavahana rulers called?
x: Satavahana rulers used matronymics, or names derived from the mother’s lineage or gotra. This practice began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.

s: What did Gautami Balasri donate?
x: Gautami Balasri donated a Buddhist vihara; Satavahana queens and women donors patronised Buddhism while kings followed Vedic religion.

s: Whose daughter was Devi Naganika, the issuer of the Naneghat inscription?
x: Naganika was the daughter of Maharathi Tranakayiro of the Amgiya family and wife of Satakarni I.

s: Under which ruler was the Satavahana centre shifted east to Dhanyakataka (Amaravati)?
x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi shifted the centre to Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) after Rudradaman's attacks.

s: With which place is Pratishthana, the principal western capital of the Satavahanas, identified?
x: Pratishthana is identified with Paithan in Maharashtra and was the principal western capital of the Satavahanas on the Godavari.

s: Which of the following was regarded as an early Satavahana political centre in the capital debate?
x: Kotilingala in Karimnagar district of Telangana has been claimed as an early Satavahana political centre. The other places are listed as sites under Satavahana rule in Andhra Pradesh.

s: With which place is Dhanyakataka, the eastern capital of the Satavahanas, identified?
x: Dhanyakataka is Amaravati (Dharanikota); Paithan (Pratishthana) was the western capital.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana centres:
1. Kotilingala, claimed as an early political centre, is in Karimnagar, Telangana.
2. Pratishthana, the principal western capital, stood on the Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kotilingala is in Karimnagar, Telangana; Pratishthana (Paithan) stood on the Godavari, not the Krishna.

s: Which place in Krishna district is regarded as the traditional early Andhra capital?
x: Srikakulam in Krishna district is the traditional early Andhra capital.

s: Upasika Bodhisri, who contributed to Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda, belongs to the reign of which Ikshvaku king?
x: Virapurushadatta's reign was the golden age of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda, when Upasika Bodhisri made her gifts.

s: Who was the 30th king in the Matsya Purana list of Satavahana rulers?
x: In the Puranic list Pulomavi III is the 30th king; Gautamiputra was the 23rd and Hala the 17th.

s: By whom was Pulomavi III, the last Satavahana king, defeated?
x: Pulomavi III, the 30th and last king, was defeated by the Ikshvaku Srisantamula and spent his last days at Myakadoni (Bellary).

s: Which Satavahana ruler had the longest reign, of 56 years?
x: The longest reign (56 years) was Satakarni II's, the 6th king; Satakarni I, the 3rd king, performed the Ashvamedha.

s: What was the position of Gautamiputra Satakarni in the Puranic list of Satavahana rulers?
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the 23rd king, the last of the early Satavahanas (rulers 1-23). '28th', found in some sources, is an error; the 17th king was Hala and the 30th and last was Pulomavi III.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Yajna Sri Satakarni — patronage of Nagarjuna
Vasishthiputra Satakarni — marriage with Rudradaman’s daughter
Pulumavi III — revival of maritime power through ship coins
x: Pulumavi III is identified as the last ruler in the Puranic sequence, whereas revival of maritime power and ship coins are associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni.

s: Which early Satavahana ruler performed the Ashvamedha and expanded into Central India?
x: Satakarni I, the greatest early ruler, performed the Ashvamedha and expanded into Central India.

s: Who was the greatest of the later Satavahana rulers and a patron of Nagarjuna?
x: Yajna Sri Satakarni (27th) was the greatest later ruler and patron of Nagarjuna.

s: What was Hala's position in the Puranic list of Satavahana kings?
x: Hala was the 17th king; Gautamiputra was the 23rd, Satakarni II the 6th and Pulomavi III the 30th.

s: Which Satavahana ruler is associated with the Sanchi torana and the longest reign?
x: Satakarni II, the 6th king, reigned 56 years and is linked with the Sanchi torana; the torana does not name Gautamiputra.

s: Srisantamula, who defeated the Satavahana king Pulomavi III, founded which dynasty in Andhra?
x: Pulomavi III was defeated by the Ikshvaku Srisantamula, founder of the Ikshvaku line that followed the Satavahanas in Andhra.

s: What does the Junagadh inscription say about the conflict between Rudradaman and the Satavahanas?
o: Defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because he was a near relative
Was defeated twice by Satakarni and later became his feudatory
Issued the first Satavahana inscription at Nasik
Built the Amaravati gateway after marrying a Satavahana princess
x: The Junagadh record states that Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because Satakarni was a near relative.

s: Which Satavahana ruler won back lost territory from the Western Kshatrapas late in the dynasty's history?
x: Yajna Sri Satakarni recovered lost territory from the Western Kshatrapas.

s: Which Satavahana ruler issued the first silver coins?
x: Satakarni I issued the first Satavahana silver coins.

s: Which of the following ruler–title pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kavivatsala was Hala's title; Gautamiputra Satakarni bore titles such as Ekabrahmana, Ekashura and Shakasanhari.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: ‘Trisamudradhipati’ is associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni, not Hala. Hala bore the title ‘Kavivatsala’.

s:
Assertion (A): Hala was associated with the title Kavivatsala.
Reason (R): Hala belonged to the Satavahana dynasty.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Hala was a Satavahana king and was called Kavivatsala, but the title comes from his love of poetry, not from his dynasty.

s: What does Gautamiputra Satakarni's title 'Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana' refer to?
o: Horses that drank the waters of three seas
Stopper of the mixing of varnas
x: Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana refers to horses drinking the waters of three seas; Varnasankarya-nirodhaka means stopper of the mixing of varnas.

s: Which one of the following titles was associated with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi?
x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi bore the titles ‘Dakshinapatheshwara’ and ‘Navanagaraswami’.

s: To whom do the titles 'Dakshinapathapati' and 'Apratihatachakra' in the Naneghat inscription belong?
x: Naneghat gives Satakarni I these titles; Dakshinapatheshwara was Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's.

s: Which title does Banabhatta's Harshacharita give to Yajna Sri Satakarni?
x: Harshacharita calls Yajna Sri Trisamudradhipati, meaning lord of three seas.

s: Gautamiputra Satakarni described himself by which pair of expressions?
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni called himself Ekabrahmana and Varnasankarya nirodhaka, the stopper of the mixing of varnas.

s: Which historian held that the Satavahanas were Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas?
x: D.C. Sircar held this view; Nilakanta Sastri distinguished tribal, dynastic and family names, and R.S. Sharma linked them with the Dravidians.

s: Who associated the Satavahanas with the original Andhra janapada?
x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao held that the Satavahanas belonged to the original Andhra janapada.

s: Who placed the original home of the Satavahanas in Vidarbha (Berar)?
x: V.V. Mirashi placed their home in Vidarbha (Berar); Gopalachari favoured Maharashtra.

s: Which scholar rejected the Bellary theory and favoured Maharashtra as the Satavahana homeland?
x: Gopalachari rejected Bellary, as no early inscription is found there, and favoured Maharashtra.

s: Who held that 'Andhra' was a tribal name, 'Satavahana' a dynastic name and 'Satakarni' a family name?
x: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri distinguished the tribal, dynastic and family names.

s: Which of the following scholar – view pairs is correctly matched?
o: V.V. Mirashi – Origin in the eastern Deccan
x: R.S. Sharma called them Dravidians; Sircar held they were Andhras, Mirashi favoured Vidarbha and Gopalachari Maharashtra.

s: Who put forward the theory, based on the Myakadoni inscription, that the original home of the Satavahanas was the Bellary region?
x: V.S. Sukthankar placed the Satavahana home in the Bellary (Kannada) region on the basis of the Myakadoni inscription; the notes follow the APPSC G2 2017 key here. Mirashi favoured Vidarbha, R.S. Sharma called them Dravidians and D.C. Sircar held they were Andhras, not Andhrabhrityas.

s: Who among the following placed the origin of the Satavahanas in the eastern Deccan (Andhra) on the basis of the Puranic 'Andhra' names?
x: Rapson (with Bhandarkar) placed the origin in the eastern Deccan; Mirashi favoured Vidarbha, Gopalachari Maharashtra, Sukthankar Bellary.

s: The Periplus refers to which aspect of the history of the Satavahanas?
o: The Kanva conquest of the Deccan
The foundation of the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara
x: The Periplus notes the conflict between the Sakas and the Satavahanas.

s: According to Ptolemy, with whom did Vasishthiputra Pulumavi clash?
x: Ptolemy records Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's clashes with Chashtana.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Puranic accounts of the Satavahanas:
1. The Matsya Purana lists 30 Satavahana kings.
2. The Matsya Purana assigns 456 years to their rule.
3. The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas give the standard chronology of 30 kings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Matsya Purana lists 30 kings and 456 years. The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention 17 kings and 272 years and are not treated as standard.

s: Which of the following works deals with the early history of the Satavahanas?
x: Dvatrimsatputtalika, like Kathasaritsagara and Pratishthanapura-kalpa, deals with early Satavahana history; Gathasaptasati does not.

s: Which foreign writer recorded that the Andhras lived in towns?
x: Megasthenes recorded that the Andhras lived in towns; Pliny wrote Natural History and Ptolemy Geography.

s: The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention how many Satavahana kings?
x: The Vayu and Vishnu Puranas give 17 kings and 272 years; the Matsya gives 30 kings and 456 years.

s: In which period does the 'long chronology' place Satavahana rule?
x: The long chronology runs from 271 BC to 174 AD; the short chronology is c. 1st c. BCE - 3rd c. CE.

s: Which Purana, with the longest list of Satavahana kings, was compiled during the reign of Yajna Sri Satakarni?
x: The Matsya Purana gives the longest list (30 kings, 456 years) and was compiled in Yajna Sri Satakarni's reign.

s: Which ruler of Kalinga sent his army to the west ignoring his contemporary, the Satavahana king Satakarni I?
x: The Hathigumpha inscription records that Kharavela of Kalinga sent an army west, ignoring his contemporary Satakarni I.

s: Apart from the Hathigumpha inscription, which text records the contact between Kalinga and the Satavahanas?
x: The Chulakalinga Jataka and the Hathigumpha inscription record the Kalinga contact in the time of Kharavela and Satakarni I.

s: Which river is called Kanhabenna in the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela?
x: Kanhabenna is the Hathigumpha name for the Krishna river, to which Kharavela sent his army.

s: According to Pliny, what was the strength of the Satavahana army?
x: Pliny mentions 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants in the Satavahana army.

s: What were the Satavahanas the first kings to do?
o: Use the Brahmi script in India
x: The Satavahanas were the first kings to issue inscriptions in Andhra itself, though Ashoka's inscriptions were earlier in time.

s: The Patagandigudem copper plates, the earliest known copper-plate land grant of south India, were issued by which Ikshvaku king?
x: The 3rd-century CE Patagandigudem plates were issued by Ikshvaku king Ehuvala Chamtamula.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Patagandigudem copper plates:
1. They belong to the Ikshvaku dynasty.
2. They record a land grant to support a Buddhist monastery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Ikshvaku Patagandigudem plates (3rd c. CE) record a royal grant for a Buddhist monastery.

s: Which Satavahana ruler is associated with the first Satavahana inscription found at Nasik?
x: The inscription associated with Krishna, also called Kanha, is regarded as the first Satavahana inscription and was found at Nasik.

s: According to the Kanheri inscription, the queen of Vasishthiputra Satakarni was the daughter of whom?
x: The Kanheri record names the queen of Vasishthiputra Satakarni as Rudradaman's daughter.

s: With whom is the Naneghat inscription associated?
x: The Naneghat inscription is associated with Satakarni I and Naganika, not Gautamiputra.

s: Which inscription is associated with the first Telugu word ‘Nagabu’?
x: The Amaravati inscription is associated with the first Telugu word ‘Nagabu’.

s: Where was the Myakadoni inscription of the last Pulumavi found?
x: Myakadoni is in Bellary, Karnataka, where Pulomavi III spent his last days.

s: Bhairavakonda, a Saiva centre with eight caves, is in which district?
x: Bhairavakonda, with eight Saiva caves, is in Nellore; Guntupalli is near Eluru.

s: Whose record is the Kodavali inscription in East Godavari?
x: Kodavali (East Godavari) is Chanda Satakarni's record; Devi Naganika issued the Naneghat inscription.

s: The Karle inscription of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi records the gift of a village for the maintenance of which group of Buddhist monks?
x: At Karle, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi granted a village for the Mahasanghika bhikshus; Gautami Balasri's Nasik cave was for the Bhadrayaniya monks.

s: In which present-day state are the earliest inscriptions of the Satavahanas found?
x: The earliest Satavahana records, Naneghat and Kanha's Nasik inscription, are in Maharashtra; later ones come from Andhra and Karnataka.

s: Which of the following pairs are among the earliest inscriptions of the Satavahanas?
x: Naneghat (Naganika) and the Nasik record of Kanha are the earliest; Amaravati, Myakadoni and Kodavali are later.

s: Which Satavahana king is named as a donor at Chinaganjam?
x: Yajnasri Satakarni is named as a donor at Chinaganjam; Amaravati records mention Pulumavi II.

s: Which Satavahana king's inscription is found on a gateway pillar of the Amaravati stupa?
x: An inscription of Pulumavi II appears on a gateway pillar of the Amaravati stupa.

s: Which Satavahana king, compiler of the Gathasaptasati, bore the title Kavivatsala?
x: Hala, the 17th king, was called Kavivatsala and compiled the Gathasaptasati in Maharashtri Prakrit; Kuntala Satakarni made Sanskrit the royal language.

s: Which poets were honoured at the court of the Satavahana king Hala?
x: Hala honoured Kumarila and Sripalita; Gunadhya and Sarvavarma were at Kuntala Satakarni's court.

s: Which of the following sets contains only early Telugu or Desi words associated with Gathasaptasati?
x: Atta, Addam, Potta and Pilla are among the early Telugu words associated with Gathasaptasati. Other recorded examples include Padi, Pandi, Ammi and Tuppu.

s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the social picture presented in Gathasaptasati?
o: Compulsory military training for all women
x: Gathasaptasati refers to sati, the absence of child marriage and the plight of wives of seafaring merchants. It does not mention compulsory military training for all women.

s: In which text are group dances and choral singing called Brundagana mentioned?
x: Gathasaptasati's social picture includes Brundagana, sugar and jaggery, house-wall paintings and hanging of criminals.

s: Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha and Reva are women contributors to the Gathasaptasati. Who among the following is another?
x: Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva or Revati, and Madhavi are identified as women contributors to the Gathasaptasati.

s:
Consider the following statements about Gathasaptasati:
1. It is a Sanskrit treatise on Jain philosophy.
2. It is an anthology of 700 gathas in Maharashtri Prakrit.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Gathasaptasati (Sattasai) is an anthology of 700 Maharashtri Prakrit gathas dealing chiefly with love, rural life and nature, not a Sanskrit Jain treatise.

s: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work to deal with which of the following?
x: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work covering all the Navarasas.

s: Why are the Desi words in the Gathasaptasati important in the history of Telugu?
o: The earliest examples of Tamil-Brahmi writing
The first official language of the Mauryan court
x: The Desi words in the Gathasaptasati are regarded as the earliest traces of Telugu, and the Satavahana period laid the foundation of the language.

s: For which of the following is Hala's Gathasaptasati an important source?
x: Gathasaptasati is an important source for Satavahana social life and describes rural life and nature, not early political history.

s: To which deity is the opening prayer of the Gathasaptasati addressed?
x: The anthology opens with a prayer to Shiva.

s: Who compiled the Gatha Saptasati, a Prakrit work that includes writing by women?
x: The Satavahana king Hala compiled the Gatha Saptasati in Prakrit; it includes verses by women poets.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gatha Saptasati:
1. It includes writing by women.
2. It was written in Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Gatha Saptasati includes writing by women, but it is in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

s: What was the relation of Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta), whose records are at Nasik and Karle, to Nahapana?
x: Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law; Ayama was his minister.

s: What was an organisation of traders and artisans of one craft, which fixed work rules, prices and wages, called?
x: Shrenis organised traders and artisans of a particular craft and regulated work, quality, prices and wages.

s: Who formed the Tilapishaka guild in the Satavahana period?
x: Tilapishaka (Tailika) were the oil-pressers' guild. Kolika were weavers, Kulara potters and Udayantrika makers of water-machines; butchers were Katika.

s: What was the head of a guild generally called in the Satavahana period?
x: A guild was headed by a Sethi or Shreshthi. Sarthavaha referred to a long-distance or foreign trader, while Gahapati was connected with urban administration.

s: What was the Satavahana guild of perfumers called?
x: Gandhika was the perfume guild. Tailika was the oil guild, Kulara the potters and Sarthavaha the long-distance traders.

s: Guilds in the Satavahana period performed which of the following economic functions?
o: They acted as banks and paid interest on deposits.
They issued only royal land grants.
They functioned exclusively as military units.
x: Guilds acted as banking institutions: they accepted deposits and paid interest, including payments benefiting monasteries.

s: Ushavadata’s Nashik inscription indicates that the weavers’ guild of Govardhana accepted deposits at which rates?
o: 2,000 karshapanas at 3% per month and 1,000 at 1% per year
1,000 karshapanas at 2% per month and 2,000 at three-fourths of 1% per year
2,000 karshapanas at 1% per month and 1,000 at three-fourths of 1% per month
3,000 karshapanas at a uniform rate of 1% per month
x: The Nashik inscription records deposits of 2,000 karshapanas at 1% monthly interest and 1,000 karshapanas at three-fourths of 1% monthly interest.

s:
Assertion (A): Guilds or Srenulu were trade associations during the Satavahana period.
Reason (R): Interest on deposits with them was 12%.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Satavahana guilds (Srenulu) were trade bodies and paid 12% interest on deposits, but the rate does not explain why they existed.

s: Irrigation devices called ghatiyantras were made by which Satavahana guild?
x: The Udayantrika guild made water-machines; Kolika were weavers.

s: How many guilds are mentioned in Satavahana inscriptions?
x: Satavahana inscriptions mention 18 guilds.

s: What was the Satavahana weavers' guild called?
x: Kolika was the Satavahana weavers' guild; Chitrameli was a medieval agriculturists' guild and Nigamalu were Ikshvaku trade guilds.

s: The Nasik inscription of Ushavadatta records a deposit of 2,000 karshapanas with the guild of which craftsmen at Govardhana?
x: Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta) deposited 2,000 karshapanas with the weavers' (Kolika) guild at Govardhana at 12% a year.

s: Ushavadata deposited money with which guild to support monks?
x: Ushavadata's deposit with the Govardhana weavers paid interest to monks.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Katantra is associated with Sharvavarman and Kundala Satakarni. Leelavati Parinayam is associated with Kutuhala, while Brihatkatha is associated with Gunadhya.

s: Who wrote the Brihatkatha, which is mentioned in connection with Satavahana literary traditions?
x: The Brihatkatha is attributed to Gunadhya and was written in Paisachi.

s: Who wrote the Brihatkatha Manjari, based on Gunadhya's Brihatkatha?
x: Kshemendra wrote the Brihatkatha Manjari, a Sanskrit version of Gunadhya's Brihatkatha. The other Sanskrit version, the Kathasaritsagara, is by Somadeva of Kashmir, not the Jain Somadeva Suri.

s: Gunadhya's Brihatkatha was organised into how many stories?
x: Brihatkatha is described as organised in seven stories; its original is lost and it mentions slavery.

s: Gunadhya was the court poet of which Satavahana king?
x: Gunadhya was Kuntala Satakarni's court poet; after losing his quarrel with Sarvavarma he wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi.

s: Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in which language?
x: Brihatkatha was written by Gunadhya in Paishachi Prakrit.

s: Lilavati Parinayam, written by Kutuhala in Prakrit, deals primarily with which event?
o: The conquest of Kalyan by the Sakas
The composition of Katantra for Kuntala Satakarni
The marriage of Hala and Lilavati at Draksharamam
The quarrel between Gunadhya and Sarvavarma at the royal court
x: Lilavati Parinayam narrates Hala's marriage to the Sinhala princess Lilavati at Draksharamam.

s: Who wrote the Jain treatise Samayasara?
x: Samayasara is Kundakundacharya's Jain treatise.

s: To whom is the Prajnaparamita shastra, a Mahayana work in Sanskrit, attributed?
x: The Prajnaparamita shastra is attributed to Nagarjuna.

s: According to legend, Gunadhya gave up Sanskrit and wrote in Paishachi after losing a dispute with whom?
x: Gunadhya lost to Sarvavarma over how fast Kuntala Satakarni could learn Sanskrit.

s: The Katantra grammar was written so that which king could learn Sanskrit quickly?
x: Sarvavarma wrote the Katantra for Kuntala Satakarni.

s: In Lilavati Parinayam, at the Bhimeswara temple of which place does Hala marry Lilavati?
x: Kutuhala places the marriage at the Bhimeswara temple, Draksharamam.

s: Who wrote the Kathasaritsagara?
x: Kathasaritsagara is by Somadeva of Kashmir (not the Jain Somadeva Suri), a Sanskrit version of Gunadhya's Brihatkatha; Kshemendra wrote Brihatkathamanjari.

s:
Consider the following statements about Gunadhya's Brihatkatha:
1. It had 7 lakh verses in 7 stories.
2. It mentions slavery.
3. Its original Paishachi text survives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Brihatkatha had 7 lakh verses in 7 stories and mentions slavery, but the original is lost; it survives in Sanskrit versions.

s: Who is the author of the Sanskrit champu 'Yashastilaka'?
x: The Jain scholar Somadeva Suri wrote the Yashastilaka (c. 959 CE); Somadeva of Kashmir wrote the Kathasaritsagara.

s: In the kingdom of which dynasty did Somadeva Suri compose the Yashastilaka?
x: Somadeva Suri composed the Yashastilaka at Gangadhara in the Vemulavada Chalukya kingdom.

s: What was the Satavahana king's council called?
x: The king's council was the Mantri Parishad; the Nigama Sabha was an urban council.

s: What was the cluster of villages headed by a Satavahana Gulmika called?
x: A Gulmika headed a Gulma, a cluster of villages, and could supervise law and order; the post later became hereditary.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the administrative hierarchy of the Satavahana state from the larger unit to the smaller unit?
x: Rashtra was a province, Ahara a district or province, Vishaya a sub-division and Grama the village unit.

s: Which of the following was regarded as the most prominent Ahara according to the Nasik inscription?
x: Govardhana was identified as the most prominent Ahara in the Nasik inscription.

s: In Satavahana administration, which officials were consulted for important decisions?
x: Visvamaatyulu were consulted for important decisions; Mahaamatyas were special officers and Rajaamatyas advisors.

s: Which officer administered regions and looked after the day-to-day military affairs of the Satavahana kingdom?
x: The Mahasenapati was the military chief who handled the day-to-day military administration of regions. The king remained the supreme commander.

s: Who was the Rajjugahaka in Satavahana administration?
x: Rajjugahaka was the land surveyor; Heranika was treasurer, Akshapatakas kept the king's orders and Pattikapala drafted land-grant inscriptions.

s: Which inscription refers to the Nigama Sabha in the context of Satavahana urban administration?
x: The Nigama Sabha, the urban council that administered towns, is referred to in the Bhattiprolu inscription (one PYQ-book explanation cites Naneghat, which is not an option here). The Allahabad pillar is Samudragupta's, Hathigumpha is Kharavela's, and Junagadh is Rudradaman's.

s: What was the Nigama Sabha of the Satavahana period?
o: An urban council that administered towns, with Gahapatis as members
A council of ministers advising the king
An assembly of guild heads that fixed coin weights
x: The Nigama Sabha was the town council that administered cities, not villages (APPSC G2 2008); its members were Gahapatis. Villages were under Gramanis/Gulmikas, the king's council was the Mantri Parishad, and guilds were headed by Shreshthis.

s: Whom did the Gaaha Pati represent in Satavahana administration?
x: The Gaaha Pati represented farmers; the Gramani headed five or ten villages and the Nigama Sabha ran towns.

s: For what could a Gramani be responsible in Satavahana administration?
x: A Gramani could oversee five or ten villages; a cluster of villages was a Gulma and distant Aharas were under military officers.

s: What was the Bhandagarika in charge of in Satavahana administration?
x: Bhandagarika looked after stores; Heranika was the treasurer.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana officers:
1. Heranika was the treasurer.
2. Rajjugahaka kept the royal stores.
3. Pattikapala drafted land-grant inscriptions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Heranika was the treasurer and Pattikapala drafted land grants; Rajjugahaka was the land surveyor, while Bhandagarika kept the stores.

s: Who administered towns and cities in Satavahana administration?
x: The Nigama Sabha ran towns; Amatyas ran the Aharas, Mahasenadhipathulu distant Aharas, and Mahaamatyas were special officers.

s: Who was the Heranika in Satavahana administration?
x: Heranika was the treasurer; Rajjugahaka was the land surveyor and Bhandagarika kept the stores.

s: Which administrative unit was run by the Amatya in Satavahana administration?
x: The Amatya was the minister or district officer who ran the Aharas (districts).

s: Who kept the records of the king's orders in Satavahana administration?
x: Akshapatakas kept records of royal orders; Heranika was treasurer, Rajjugahaka surveyor, Bhandagarika in charge of stores.

s: Which Satavahana officer looked after the police?
x: Pradeshika was the police officer; Pattikapala drafted land-grant inscriptions.

s: Who was the village headman in Satavahana administration?
x: The Gramika was the village headman; a Gramani was over 5 or 10 villages.

s: Which ruler is associated with ship-motif coins and the extension of Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra?
x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi issued ship-motif coins and extended Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra.

s: Kotilingala in Karimnagar district is known for the coins of which Satavahana ruler?
x: Coins of the founder Simuka, with the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata', have been found at Kotilingala in Telangana.

s: What does the Ujjain symbol on the reverse of Satavahana coins look like?
o: a circle divided into eight segments
x: The Ujjain symbol is described as a cross with four circles and appears on the reverse of Satavahana coins.

s: Which of the following was part of Gautamiputra Satakarni's monetary policy?
o: Issuing only bilingual coins in Greek and Latin
Replacing all silver coins with gold coins
x: Gautamiputra Satakarni restruck the silver coins of Nahapana.

s: What do the portrait coins of the Satavahana period represent?
o: a Gupta innovation copied by the Satavahanas
an indigenous innovation, beginning with Gautamiputra Satakarni
a Roman practice introduced only under Yajna Sri Satakarni
a practice restricted to copper coins of Hala
x: Portrait coins are regarded as an indigenous innovation, and their issue began with Gautamiputra Satakarni. Silver portrait coins became common after him.

s: Bilingual silver portrait coins of later Satavahana rulers carried which languages on their two sides?
x: The bilingual silver portrait coins carried Prakrit on one side and a Dravidian language on the other.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana ship-motif coins:
1. Later Satavahana rulers continued to issue them.
2. They are associated with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Ship-motif coins are associated with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni, and no later ruler issued them.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana coinage:
1. The silver coin was called a karshapana.
2. One suvarna was equal to 35 karshapanas.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The silver coin was called a karshapana, and one suvarna was equivalent to 35 karshapanas.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana coin legends:
1. They were written in Kharosthi script.
2. They were generally in Prakrit.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Satavahana coin legends were generally in Prakrit and written in Brahmi, not Kharosthi.

s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana coinage:
1. Lead was the most commonly used metal.
2. Gold coins were issued for overseas trade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Lead was the most common metal; the Satavahanas issued no gold coins and used gold only as bullion.

s: Which dynasty issued lead, copper and bronze coins with bull and lion symbols?
x: The Pallavas issued lead, copper and bronze coins with bull and lion symbols.

s: Where have coins of the founder Simuka bearing the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata' been found?
x: Kotilingala (Karimnagar, Telangana) yielded Simuka's coins with the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata'; Kondapur (Medak) is known as a Satavahana mint site.

s: With which ruler did Satavahana portrait coins begin?
x: Portrait coins, an indigenous innovation, began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.

s: Simuka, the founder of Satavahana rule, issued coins bearing which legend?
x: Coins of the founder Simuka found at Kotilingala carry the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata'.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Satavahana coinage?
o: Lead was the most commonly used metal
Coin legends were in Prakrit and Brahmi
Iron coins with a thin copper coating were issued
x: Iron coins with a thin copper coating belong to the Ikshvakus, not the Satavahanas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. No ruler after the Satavahanas issued ship-motif coins.
2. The Phanigiri pot of lead coins belongs to the Ikshvakus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ship-motif coins ended with the Satavahanas; the Phanigiri pot of 3,730 lead coins is Ikshvaku.

s: Which place in Medak district has been identified as a Satavahana mint site?
x: Kondapur in Medak is a Satavahana mint site; Kotilingala in Karimnagar is known for Simuka's coins.

s: Which of the following metals was NOT used for Satavahana coins?
x: Satavahana coins were of lead (most common), copper, bronze, silver and potin; gold and nickel were not used.

s: Who is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language during the Satavahana period?
x: Kuntala Satakarni, regarded as the thirteenth Satavahana king, is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language.

s: Who called Telugu the “Italian of the East”?
x: The British called Telugu the "Italian of the East", because, like Italian, its words end in vowels; the phrase goes back to the Venetian traveller Niccolo de Conti.

s: Desi Bhaasha, the language of common people in the Satavahana period, belonged to which language family?
x: Desi Bhaasha, used by common people, belonged to the Dravidian family.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the development of Sanskrit and Telugu in the Deccan?
o: The Nasik Prasasti is the first complete Sanskrit inscription
Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus
'Nagabu' is identified as the first Telugu word, in the Amaravati inscription
x: The Nasik Prasasti is in Prakrit; Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is regarded as the first complete Sanskrit inscription.

s: The Gundaram Forest inscriptions associated with the Satavahana period were found in which present-day location?
x: Under review: the Satavahana-era inscriptions found by the ASI in 2025 are in the Gundaram reserve forest of Peddapalli district (May 2025); none of the options is correct.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Telugu was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi. Satavahana common people spoke Desi Bhaasha, the Salankayanas used Sanskrit and Sangam literature was in Tamil.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Prakrit was the official language of the Satavahanas.
Three of the eight Salankayana inscriptions were in Prakrit.
Telugu became the official language of Andhra Pradesh from 1956.
Early Ikshvaku inscriptions were in Prakrit.
x: Option C is incorrect: Telugu became the official language of Andhra Pradesh in 1966, not 1956. Prakrit as the Satavahana official language, three Prakrit Salankayana inscriptions and Prakrit early Ikshvaku inscriptions are right.

s: The Telugu script developed from which source?
x: The Telugu script developed from Brahmi, through the Bhattiprolu and later Telugu-Kannada scripts. Prakrit and Pali are languages, not scripts.

s: Under which dynasty did Sanskrit replace Prakrit as the official language?
x: Sanskrit replaced Prakrit under the Salankayanas; the Satavahanas and early Ikshvakus used Prakrit.

s: Which is the first complete Sanskrit inscription?
x: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is the first complete Sanskrit inscription.

s: Which Telugu word occurs in the Myakadoni inscription of Pulumavi?
x: Myakadoni has 'Vepuru'; 'Nagabu' is from Amaravati and 'Atta', 'Pilla' are Desi words in the Gathasaptasati.

s: From which year did Telugu become the official language of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Telugu became AP's official language in 1966, not 1956.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Guntupalli was associated with copper and iron, not gold. Guduru, Vinukonda and Palnadu were associated respectively with fine cotton, metal and diamonds.

s: For what was Guntupalli known in the Satavahana period?
x: Guntupalli yielded copper and iron, not gold; Palnadu gave diamonds and Guduru fine cotton.

s: Which of the following sets contains only towns associated with the Satavahana urban network?
x: Barukaccha, Sopara, Kalyan and Govardhana are included among the major Satavahana towns. The other sets combine urban centres from different historical contexts.

s: By what expression were the Satavahanas famed as road builders?
x: Mahapatha nirmatalu means builders or makers of great roads and is associated with the Satavahanas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Satavahana inland trade?
o: Pratishthana was only a religious settlement and not a trade centre.
Tagara was an emporium linked to coastal ports.
Pratishthana was both a capital and an inland trade centre.
x: Pratishthana was both a capital and an inland trade centre, so calling it only a religious settlement is wrong.

s: Which Satavahana port was known in Greek accounts as Barygaza?
x: Bharuch was known as Barygaza. It came under Satavahana control after the defeat of Nahapana.

s: Which of the following ports was destroyed by the Sakas, according to the Periplus?
x: The Periplus records that Kalyan was destroyed by the Sakas. Kantakasela and Maisolia were east-coast ports, while Motupalli belonged to a later Eastern Chalukya context.

s: Which one of the following was regarded as the only east-coast port of the Satavahana period in the Periplus?
x: Koddura, identified with the Gudur area in Krishna, was described in the Periplus as the only east-coast port.

s: Which of the following port–identification pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kantakossyla is identified with Ghantasala. Maisolia is Machilipatnam, Koddura the Gudur area and Dhanyakataka Amaravati/Dharanikota.

s: Which route correctly represents the inland commercial connection from Ujjain to Bharuch?
x: The inland route from Ujjain to Bharuch passed through Paithan and Tagara.

s: On the main route from the west coast into the Deccan, through which pass was Kalyan linked to Junnar?
x: The route ran Kalyan - Naneghat pass - Junnar - Paithan.

s: Which of the following port – identification pairs is correctly matched?
x: Maisolia is Machilipatnam; Kantakossyla is Ghantasala, Koddura is the Gudur area and Vengipuram is Pedavegi.

s: With which place is Vengipuram of the Satavahana period identified?
x: Vengipuram is Pedavegi near Eluru; Vijayapuri is Nagarjunakonda.

s: What is the present name of Bharukachha, the Satavahana-period west-coast port?
x: Bharukachha was Bharuch in Gujarat, while Sopara and Kalyan were west-coast ports in Maharashtra.

s: Under which dynasty did Motupalli rise as a port?
x: Motupalli was not a Satavahana port; it rose later under the Kakatiyas. Satavahana ports included Kodur, Kalyan and Sopara.

s: Where have Roman coins of Satavahana-period trade been found?
x: Roman coins have been found at Bhattiprolu and Nagarjunakonda. The gold coin of Constantine found at Kudali Sangameswaram belongs to a later period.

s: Who described the drain of Roman gold and referred to fine cloth in connection with Indian trade?
o: The anonymous author of the Periplus
x: Pliny, writing in Latin in Natural History, referred to the drain of Roman gold and fine cloth. Ptolemy and the Periplus supplied other commercial references.
